9123: Rotary Club of Grande Prairie campground, built from 1967 on land the city provided; all of its profits go back into the community.  It has 21 full-service 30-amp sites, 16 power-and-water 50-amp pull-throughs and 24 power-and-water back-ins (20 of them 30-amp and 4 50-amp), and the section of sites 22 to 41 has fire pits (except at 34) and a playground.  A grocery store and a casino are across the street, and the Muskoseepi Park walking trails are at hand.  No tents; bookings for the Bear Creek Folk Festival weekend are non-refundable. --Claude
9140: Private campground near Tofield, 30 minutes east of Edmonton, run by hosts Bernie and Krystina, with well-treed private sites, a heated pool, a playground and on-site security.  Each site has power, a picnic table and a fire pit; campers fill their water tanks at the pool house on the way in and use the sani-dump on the way out.  Generators are not permitted.  Weekends take a 2-night minimum and long weekends 3.  In 2026 the campground warned that stays after October 1 depend on the weather. --Claude
9144: RV resort 15 minutes north of Edmonton near Gibbons and Jurassic Forest, Canada's largest animatronic dinosaur park; guests have on-site access to the Goose Hummock Golf Resort's 18-hole championship course and beach volleyball courts, and The Marsh banquet hall holds up to 188.  Sites have gravel pads, fire pits and picnic tables, and there are public washrooms.  Groceries are 5 minutes away in Gibbons; the main gate closes at 9 p.m. --Claude
9146: RV park 5 minutes southwest of Bonnyville, near Highway 28 and the Bonnyville Golf Club, for work and leisure stays; its 40 by 60 ft lots have treated water and winterized lines, and it offers an off-leash dog park, firewood, a backup generator, snow removal and mail forwarding. --Claude
9225: Town of Battleford campground at the south end of town, next to Fort Battleford, with 36 full-service and 38 electrical sites, toilets, a service centre and picnic areas, including an enclosed picnic shelter to rent.  Phone bookings are taken only during the office's hours, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily in season. --Claude
9226: Town of Eston campground steps from the town's outdoor pool, open from late June to the end of August, and the fairgrounds.  Fire pits are not provided, and a town alarm sounds daily at noon, 6 p.m. and 9 p.m.  Weekly and monthly rates are available. --Claude
9227: Regional park in the South Saskatchewan River valley south of Eston, beside the river, with an irrigated nine-hole grass-greens golf course and licensed clubhouse, an outdoor pool, mini golf, two ball diamonds, a playground and a hall to rent; the pool and concession open in July and August.  It has 18 full-service sites, 20 15-amp electric sites and 10 non-serviced sites plus group camping; every site has a picnic table and a pole barbecue or fire pit.  The campground taps are not drinking water, which is sold at the clubhouse and concession.  There is no boat launch (the nearest is at the ferry, about 10 km away), but boats can be beached beside the park. --Claude
9261: Regional park on the shores of Nickle Lake and the Souris River near Weyburn, where tall poplars line the road in and each area has a playground; there are shelters and benches along the shoreline, a groomed sandy beach and roped-off swimming area (no lifeguard), an 18-hole mini golf course and, new in 2026, a canteen.  Its 342 sites are 16 tent, 55 full-service and 271 30-amp power-and-water sites, with group camping in a secluded bay and at Crescent Point; some partial-service sites in Riverview are pull-throughs.  Two boat launches and a floating dock serve the lake, which holds walleye, perch and pike, is stocked from time to time and has a fish-cleaning area.  An 18-hole golf course is 3 miles away. --Claude
9279: The Town of Eastend's in-town campground on the west side of town beside the Frenchman River, where you can fish or launch a kayak; it is next to a playground, ball diamonds, the swimming pool and splash park and the Streambank Golf Course, and has barbecues, picnic tables and a sheltered cook area.  Of its 43 sites (site 12 is not available), 17 are full-service, 24 have power and water and 1 has no service.  The 2026 season started on the May long weekend; a camp manager is on site from May to September. --Claude
9288: Regional park at Wynyard's west entrance, 2.5 km south of the Yellowhead Highway on Grid 640, quiet and well treed; its reservoir, behind the old CPR dam, is aerated and holds rainbow trout (canoes, kayaks and electric-powered boats are allowed; fishing needs a provincial licence).  Campers have barbecues and free firewood; the park's water is not drinkable, and a coin-operated potable water station is at the Town Shop in Wynyard.  There is no full-time attendant: the facilities are cleaned and restocked once a day.  Camping runs from the Victoria Day long weekend to the end of September, and the trails stay open all year. --Claude
9297: City of North Battleford campground, a quiet 20-acre RV park east of the city with quick access to city attractions and nearby lakes; it has a dog run and pet area, fire pits and firewood, a pavilion, a playground and a sports field.  Of its sites, 41 are fully serviced and 20 non-serviced. --Claude
9414: Family resort at Oak Lake Beach whose full-service RV sites are let both seasonally and nightly, steps from its championship 18-hole golf course; it has two heated outdoor pools, an 18-hole mini golf course, a Creemee ice cream and take-out stand, a licensed restaurant at the golf clubhouse, beach access, a marina, playgrounds, Wi-Fi hotspots in key areas and planned events all summer.  It also rents four cabins and an RV.  Guests must be 25 or older to reserve. --Claude
9421: Prairie campground just outside Brandon, owned and operated by Gambler First Nation, with spacious RV and tent sites, full-service sites, a playground and an on-site manager, and easy access from Highway 1. --Claude
9794: City of Genesee RV park in the heart of town, in the Palouse halfway between Moscow and Lewiston, beside Cow Creek and close to shops and dining; its roomy sites have concrete pads and picnic tables, and it has free garbage disposal, a playground, a restaurant and a sports field, and the Cow Creek Wetland Trail nearby for walks and birdwatching. --Claude
9822: Quiet, tree-shaded RV park in Mountain Home, 35 minutes from Boise and close to I-84, with private sites among mature trees; it takes overnighters as well as contract workers and longer-term guests.  Campspot lists its bathrooms, showers and laundry as seasonal.  The 2.5-mile Greenbelt is nearby, and the Mountain Home Golf Course is a block away. --Claude
9824: Family-owned resort under 25 minutes' drive north of Mountain Home, near Little Camas Reservoir and within 20 minutes of the Anderson Reservoir boat launch and the South Fork of the Boise River.  It has a swimming pool, 9-hole mini golf, disc golf, a 3-hole mountain links golf course, horseshoes, walking and biking trails and a non-motorized youth dirt bike track, plus cabins and tent sites; one extra tent is allowed in an RV site, and trailer and UTV storage is offered.  Guests must be 21 to book, and the Memorial Day, July 4 and Labor Day weekends take a 2-night minimum. --Claude
9841: RV park on the Payette River in Cascade whose sites have cement pads and picnic tables; not every site has a fire pit, but a community fire pit by the river comes with firewood.  It has a nature trail, a dog park, pickleball, horseshoes and a remodeled rec room, and the store sells firewood, ice, snacks, basic RV parts and propane refills.  Guests can learn to carve a totem pole or take classes from onsite artisans.  It also has rustic cabins, yurts and tent sites. --Claude
9846: Family RV park on the Payette River in Cascade, within a mile of Lake Cascade, started in 1992 and now run by the founders' daughter and her husband; it serves free cinnamon rolls by the river on Saturday mornings and has a private barbecue area and fire pit, free kayak use and cabins to rent. --Claude
10146: Shady RV park in the heart of Kanab near Navajo sandstone cliffs, with a community fire pit and a dog area; guests must be 21 to book, each site takes up to 4 people, and the park is smoke-free. --Claude
10166: Circleville RV Park and its Kountry Store, right off US-89 in the town of Circleville in south-central Utah, within reach of Bryce Canyon, Zion, Capitol Reef and the Grand Canyon's North Rim; its grass and gravel sites, shaded by mature trees or in full sun, have campfire rings, and the store and gift shop (sporting goods, fishing and hunting supplies, ATV accessories, snacks) also serves Piute County.  It is a base for ATV and UTV riding, fishing and hunting; RV and ATV storage is offered for a fee, and two restaurants and an auto repair shop are within walking distance. --Claude
10182: Working cattle ranch of Ben Mead and his daughter Carla in Nine Mile Canyon, 24 paved miles up Nine Mile Canyon Road from Wellington and a gateway to the canyon's petroglyphs; its campgrounds are the only camping allowed in the canyon.  Its campgrounds sit beside Nine Mile Creek with plenty of shade and green grass; every site has a picnic table and a fire pit or ring, and every campground a spring-water faucet.  Kokopelli is best for RVs, trailers and vans, Cottonwood Hollow is mostly for tents, small vans and truck campers, and the Turnouts are pull-throughs.  Showers ($3) are at the main ranch, and generators are off from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. (9 p.m. in fall).  The ranch also rents settler cabins rebuilt on the property and bed-and-breakfast rooms.  There is no cell service in the 50-mile canyon, and Wi-Fi only around the main house. --Claude
10251: Park run by Vista Recreation on a 282-acre island in Lower Granite Lake on the Snake River near Clarkston, the gateway to the Hells Canyon Recreation Area; the campground is spacious and shady, with a swimming beach, a boat launch, five docks and a short walk to Maya Lin's Listening Circle.  Kayaking and windsurfing on the lake are popular. --Claude
10458: Lewis County PUD campground at Leonard “Bud” Allen Park, over 110 acres, 15 miles east of Morton and central to Mount St. Helens, Mount Rainier and the Gifford Pinchot National Forest.  It has 41 RV sites with electric and water hookups in Areas A and D, 21 tent sites, 6 group tent sites and a group RV site, plus picnic shelters, barbecues, baseball, soccer and volleyball, disc golf, horseshoes, nature trails, a playground and a boat launch.  The dump station is for registered campers only, and RV chemicals must not be used in holding tanks (the campground is on a septic system).  The gates are open from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.; a 25% disability discount is given with a placard or pass. --Claude
10521: Family-owned RV and tent resort in the heart of Westport, close to the beaches, parks, restaurants, shops, marina and docks; it has a 2,400 sq ft clubhouse to rent, a secluded tent area, three rental cabins, a fish-cleaning station, a heated outdoor pool, horseshoe pits, a playground and campfire containers, and sells propane, ice and firewood.  A special monthly rate is available on request. --Claude
